models.summary: Sea level is fit to temperature, its square, and a time trend on annual data, then differenced once after a stationarity test. The printed fit reads 8.826 minus 2.086 on the temperature change plus 0.07 on its square and 0.003 on time; the watermark breaks the line, so the coefficients are recorded as printed. Land is flattened to a circle because altitude is small against the width of a territory. A cited rule, 35 cm of rise floods one kilometre, turns the rise into a ring of drowned land. People are split in two: half the world population spread evenly inside 150 km of a coast, the rest inland, with a separate count once the flood crosses that band.

models.summary: Cultural value is a weighted sum of three carriers named from the literature: heritage, landscape, and custom. Heritage is priced from the World Heritage List and lender valuations. Landscape value is tourism revenue summed over a finite life, optionally discounted. Custom, defended as cohesion and identity and therefore hard to price, is taken as a fraction of the flooded country's product. For the Maldives the weights are 0.26, 0.69 and 0.05, local remains are valued at 17.524 billion Rufiyaa, tourism at 6.74 billion a year over 75 years, and the total is 349.734 billion Rufiyaa, about 22.462 billion US dollars.

models.summary: Eight indicators under two criterion layers score how well a host matches a drowning country. Rights and development use the UN human development index and a three-level treatment score. Natural match uses gaps in decade-average temperature, precipitation, and the coast-to-border ratio. Culture uses a distance between regime types, a five-to-one religion score, and a four-to-one language score. Scores build a comparison matrix, weights follow, and a consistency ratio gates the result. For the Maldives the top layer gives a largest eigenvalue of 3.007 and a ratio of 0.0068, and Malaysia, India and Indonesia rank highest.

models.summary: Stress on a host combines inflation, unemployment, crime, per-capita product growth and population growth with the refugee share of population. All series are mapped to the interval from 1 to 2. Harmful indicators are multiplied by the squared refugee share and helpful ones divide it, then both are mapped back to a common range. Weights are given as 2, 1, 2, 0.5, 1 in the text, while the appendix code uses 2, 2, 2, 1, 2. The square is defended by loss aversion: disgust rises faster than the refugee share. The line is read off elections. The index was about 13 when the 2016 US administration changed, about 15 and 18 for the 2018 Italian and Hungarian results, and the paper sets the world line near 12 because parties lag the public.

models.summary: A nonlinear program joins the host ranking and the stress index. It maximizes the welfare of the displaced, each person weighted by the host's match score, subject to a deadline, to stress staying under the line in every host and year, and to the shares summing to one. Because welfare rises the more people reach a higher-ranked host, the solve splits in two: the most each host can take each year without crossing the line, then the shares. Urgency pulls in more countries, but low-ranked hosts protect culture badly, so earlier action is preferred. With time to spare only Malaysia takes the Maldivians, 70 to 80 thousand a year over seven years. Forced inside five years, India joins at 40 to 50 thousand.

models.summary: The bill is the headcount times a per-person resettlement cost that depends on the treatment offered, plus a fraction of the cultural loss spent on protection. National treatment is priced at 6,000 dollars a person. For the Maldives, 552,147 people and 5 percent of 22.462 billion dollars of culture are combined; the summary states the bill as about 3.43 billion, while the case text's arithmetic points much higher, and the clash is recorded rather than resolved. Shares follow historical emissions, scaled by an incentive coefficient defined as the geometric mean of the change in emissions per person over the reviewed years, so recent cuts reduce a state's bill. The payers are the G20, chosen for holding about 85 percent of world product.

models.summary: For a shock too fast for the normal process, shelters are scored on three things: closeness of capitals, the ratio of the two populations, and the host's area. Distance and the population ratio are inverted so every indicator points the same way, then each is scaled by its range to sit between zero and one. Weights come from the literature. Countries are filled from the top of the ranking, each capped at a share of its own population, and once a country hits the cap the remainder is reallocated by score. For a Japan shock hitting half the population the cap is raised 2.5 times, and China, Russia and South Korea absorb everyone.
